newsitem.title: USA: U.S. study finds heart attack-education link.
newsitem.headline: U.S. study finds heart attack-education link.

text.p: People without a high school education may be twice as likely to have a heart attack triggered by anger than people who have at least some college education, according to a study released on Sunday.

"The risk of having a myocardial infarction (heart attack) triggered by isolated episodes of anger declined consistently and significantly with increasing levels of educational attainment," said the report from Harvard Medical School.
The study, based on a look at more than 1,600 patients who had suffered heart attacks, appeared in the Archives of Internal Medicine, a publication of the American Medical Association.
The heart attack victims were interviewed an average of four days after they were stricken.

Nearly 4 percent of the patients who did not have high school diplomas reported feeling "very angry, furious or enraged" two hours prior to their heart attack compared to 2.2 percent of patients who had finished high school and 1.7 percent with at least some college education.
The report did not speculate on why education might have a protective effect and said more research is needed in the area.
